security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel reads stval into frame->tf_stval (exception.S:110-111) without first ensuring senvcfg.PME=0 to disable pointer masking. If prior boot stages (M-mode firmware, UEFI, or previous kernel) left senvcfg.PME=1, the hardware applies pointer masking to the faulting address written to stval. In trap.c page_fault_handler, the masked stval is consumed raw: checked with VIRT_IS_VALID (which interprets sign-extended masked addresses as illegal), truncated to va=trunc_page(stval) for pmap lookups, and passed as si_addr to userspace signals. For kernel-mode faults at line 245, if PMM=0 zeroes upper bits of a kernel address, the masked stval falls below VM_MIN_KERNEL_ADDRESS, causing the fault to be routed to the user map instead of the kernel map.
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD kernel never initializes senvcfg, so if firmware left pointer masking enabled, hardware-masked stval values break VIRT_IS_VALID address checks, causing spurious SIGSEGV for userspace or kernel panic for kernel-mode faults misrouted to user map

findings.finding: Hardware stval CSR is read directly via csrr and stored into tf_stval without consulting senvcfg.PME, but since the kernel never writes senvcfg (zero PMLEN on reset), pointer masking is never enabled for S-mode, so stval always holds the raw unmasked VA.
stval is consumed raw from the trapframe without PMLEN-aware unmasking. This is safe because the kernel never enables pointer masking (no senvcfg write anywhere in the codebase, PMLEN=0 after reset).

VIRT_IS_VALID(stval) for usermode checks uses raw stval. If PMLEN were non-zero and PMM=0 (zeroing upper bits), a sign-extended masked address could be misclassified as invalid. But PMLEN=0 in practice.

Kernel-mode stval compared against VM_MIN_KERNEL_ADDRESS (0xffffffc000000000) to choose kernel_map vs user map. If PMLEN were non-zero and PMM=0 zeroed upper bits of a kernel VA, the masked stval would fall below VM_MIN_KERNEL_ADDRESS, routing the fault to the wrong map. But PMLEN=0 in practice.
trunc_page(stval) truncates raw stval for pmap lookups. If PMLEN were non-zero and PMM=0, the truncated page address could misalign due to masked upper bits. But PMLEN=0 in practice.
Masked stval passed as si_addr to userspace via call_trapsignal. If PMLEN were non-zero, userspace would receive a corrupted fault address. But PMLEN=0 in practice.
Fatal kernel page fault panic prints masked stval. Minor forensic impact if PMLEN were non-zero. But PMLEN=0 in practice.
findings.snippet: panic("Fatal page fault at %#lx: %#lx", frame->tf_sepc, stval);

findings.finding: Boot code sets up stvec, satp, sscratch, and page tables but never configures senvcfg. Pointer masking remains disabled (PMLEN=0) across the full boot-to-kernel transition. No violation.
Hypervisor writes only HENVCFG_STCE (timer delegation). No PMLEN or PMM bits are set in henvcfg. Guest senvcfg slot exists in struct hypcsr (riscv.h:67) but is never read/written — dead field.
Only HENVCFG_* bitfields are defined (STCE, PBMTE, CBZE, CBCFE, CBIE, FIOM). No SENVCFG_PMM, SENVCFG_PMLEN, or any pointer-masking bit definitions exist — confirming zero PM support.
CSR definitions exist for sstatus/sie/stvec/sscratch/sepc/scause/stval/sip/satp only. No CSR_SENVCFG, CSR_MENVCFG, or CSR_HENVCFG register numbers — confirming no envcfg CSR access possible.
ISA extension parser recognizes sstc/svnapot/svpbmt/svinval/sscofpmf only. No Ss npm (pointer masking) extension check — PM is not advertised to the kernel, so no PM hardware path is activated.
